raw.title: Staff Applied AI Engineer
raw.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape how Pleo builds AI-powered product features, working alongside software engineers, data engineers and data scientists to take ideas from prototype to production. Pleo has over 40,000 customers and a decade of unique spend data — an incredible foundation to build on. Your mission will be to harness this data to create real product value.

 

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You'll be one of the first hires in our Data & AI Products team but, rest assured, you will not be working solo! You will work very closely with other Engineers and Data Scientists, each bringing distinctive skills while you bring applied AI engineering and data context. Together, the team covers the full chain from data to shipped product.

Your core focus is on building and shipping AI-powered features, with a strong collaborative element across Product Engineering, AI Platform, and Data & ML Platform teams.

 

What you’ll be doing

As a Staff Applied AI Engineer you will:

  • Build and ship multiple AI-powered product features, setting the bar for delivery at Pleo, across agentic workflows, spend intelligence, automated actions, and more.

  • Bring deep applied AI expertise and strong judgment on trade-offs (quality vs latency/cost, build vs buy, agent patterns vs simpler approaches) and help teams avoid hype-driven decisions.

  • Work directly with Product, Design, Engineering, and business stakeholders to advise and prioritise on what's actually worth building. You aren't just implementing specs, you're discovering and defining the product.

  • Own the evaluation, monitoring, and operationalisation of AI features: setting up evals, tracking drift and performance, and managing prompt changes safely in production. You will help establish how Pleo does this at scale and own the development in production.

  • Act as a design partner to the GenAI Core platform team: challenge decisions with evidence from real feature delivery, bring clear requirements, and validate platform choices in production.

  • Establish and enforce practical standards for AI feature delivery in product squads (evaluation strategy, monitoring expectations, safe prompt/versioning practices, privacy & safety guardrails) using GenAI Platform tooling (not building the platform itself).

  • Upskill the team through mentorship, reviews, pairing, and lightweight playbooks that make other engineers faster.

 

What you bring

You will thrive in this role if you have:

  • Proven experience shipping multiple GenAI features into production, at scale in a customer-facing product. You've moved past prototype phases and ideally have experience shipping multi-step, tool-using agents in a user-facing product.

  • The ability to translate complex business challenges and product visions into scalable AI solutions. In other words, you can autonomously scope, design and build.

  • Deep applied AI judgment: you can reason about evaluation, retrieval quality, tool use, failure modes, and what is/isn’t worth building.

  • Experience applying evaluation and observability to LLM systems (tests, golden sets, online metrics, monitoring) and using those signals to iterate.

  • Strong understanding of privacy and security concerns when building LLM applications: prompt injection, handling PII and data leakage risk.

  • Solid experience with the modern AI stack including Vector DBs, orchestration and durable execution frameworks, and LLM APIs.

  • Experience building APIs, services and data retrieval pipelines (RAG, vector search etc) to feed data into LLMs.

  • Deep proficiency with Python for both data and ML engineering, SQL and major cloud providers.

  • An extensive background in traditional ML engineering and a deep understanding of how to architect and build data systems for reliable and scalable production-use.

  • Ability to influence cross-functionally with Product/Design/Engineering and bring teams along on decisions.

To share extra context, our current tech stack includes GCP, BigQuery, Airflow, Python, SQL on the Data side and AWS, Kotlin, Javascript, Typescript on the Product side while our infrastructure is containerised with Kubernetes. Experience across those technologies or languages would be considered a bonus.

 

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You have strong product instincts and build with the user in mind. You understand that a model is only as good as the problem it solves.

  • You have moved past prototyping and have a deep understanding of the realities of LLMOps, data retrieval, prompt and context engineering, as well as model evaluation in production.

  • You don't just call APIs, you understand the data feeding the AI system and can reason about data quality, architecture, and retrieval without needing a dedicated data engineer beside you at all times.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You want to focus on research and algorithm development. We need someone who cares about shipping solutions to production right now, turning AI concepts into functional features that solve real financial problems today.

  • You need a perfectly groomed backlog, structured tooling and pre-defined specs. We expect our Staff Engineers to be able to navigate ambiguity, to autonomously scope solutions and build any new tooling that might be required.

  • You can't explain complex AI trade-offs to a CEO or a designer without losing them in the weeds. You work well with stakeholders who are very technically or commercially focused.

 

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Familiarise yourself with our codebase, tooling and roadmap.

  • Partner with our Principal Engineer to define and own our approach to AI feature development.

  • Contribute to shaping the roadmap for tooling and features developed by our GenAI Core team.

  • Collaborate with Product and Data teams to ship a first feature to production

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills!

The location

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work.

We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

 

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Technical screening: A 15 to 30 minute call with our Talent Partner to check your knowledge of key technical topics

  3. System design interview: A 75-minute practical session with our engineers focusing on scoping and designing an AI feature

  4. Live coding interview: A 75-minute practical session with our engineers focusing on implementing your solution.

  5. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation to deep dive into your knowledge and experience.

  6. Final interview: A leadership interview focusing on your behavioural, communication and collaboration skills.

 

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

  • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

  • Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • Profile to role fit: this is neither a research-driven nor a traditional data or software engineering role. We're looking for someone with proven experience shipping customer-facing AI products who can also confidently operate at Staff level in a SaaS organisation. This means we'll be looking for evidence that you can own fairly complex initiatives that have organisation-wide impacts beyond just building and shipping.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

  • You have strong product instincts and build with the user in mind. You understand that a model is only as good as the problem it solves.

  • You have moved past prototyping and have a deep understanding of the realities of LLMOps, data retrieval, prompt and context engineering, as well as model evaluation in production.

  • You don't just call APIs, you understand the data feeding the AI system and can reason about data quality, architecture, and retrieval without needing a dedicated data engineer beside you at all times.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You want to focus on research and algorithm development. We need someone who cares about shipping solutions to production right now, turning AI concepts into functional features that solve real financial problems today.

  • You need a perfectly groomed backlog, structured tooling and pre-defined specs. We expect our Staff Engineers to be able to navigate ambiguity, to autonomously scope solutions and build any new tooling that might be required.

  • You can't explain complex AI trade-offs to a CEO or a designer without losing them in the weeds. You work well with stakeholders who are very technically or commercially focused.

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Familiarise yourself with our codebase, tooling and roadmap.

  • Partner with our Principal Engineer to define and own our approach to AI feature development.

  • Contribute to shaping the roadmap for tooling and features developed by our GenAI Core team.

  • Collaborate with Product and Data teams to ship a first feature to production

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills!

The location

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work.

We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Technical screening: A 15 to 30 minute call with our Talent Partner to check your knowledge of key technical topics

  3. System design interview: A 75-minute practical session with our engineers focusing on scoping and designing an AI feature

  4. Live coding interview: A 75-minute practical session with our engineers focusing on implementing your solution.

  5. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation to deep dive into your knowledge and experience.

  6. Final interview: A leadership interview focusing on your behavioural, communication and collaboration skills.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

  • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

  • Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • Profile to role fit: this is neither a research-driven nor a traditional data or software engineering role. We're looking for someone with proven experience shipping customer-facing AI products who can also confidently operate at Staff level in a SaaS organisation. This means we'll be looking for evidence that you can own fairly complex initiatives that have organisation-wide impacts beyond just building and shipping.

Partnerships at Duffel

Partnerships owns Duffel’s global supply strategy across airlines, hotels, cars and emerging travel verticals. We work directly with suppliers to unlock high quality content, build commercial frameworks, and ensure our platform scales with the industry.

As our airline portfolio grows, so does the complexity of managing relationships, distribution updates and commercial structures. This role sits at the centre of that system, ensuring everything runs smoothly day to day.

About this role & Why it matters

This role is for someone who enjoys bringing structure to complex, fast-moving environments and making things happen. Airlines are a core part of Duffel’s platform, and how we manage those relationships directly impacts our ability to grow.

You’ll work closely with the Head of Partnerships to keep Duffel’s airline relationships and pipeline moving, ensuring partners are supported, internal teams are aligned, and priorities are executed. You’ll act as the connective layer between airlines and Duffel’s internal teams, translating partner conversations into clear actions and making sure nothing falls through the cracks.

This role plays a central part in keeping partnership operations running effectively, ensuring we stay aligned with airlines while moving quickly internally. You’ll gain hands-on exposure to modern airline distribution, working closely with global carriers and internal teams to see how partnerships translate into real product and commercial outcomes. It’s a role with strong visibility, where high-quality execution makes a meaningful impact on how Duffel operates and scales.

What we’re looking for in you

  • Experience: Previous experience in account management, partnerships, or commercial operations. Ability to operate independently and follow through on tasks, while knowing when to escalate.

  • Industry Knowledge (Nice to have): Experience in the travel industry, particularly airlines or distribution, with familiarity with GDS, NDC or airline commercial models.

  • Data Literacy: Comfort working with data and reporting, with the ability to interpret performance and spot trends. Exposure to tools like SQL, Metabase, or similar analytics platforms is a plus.

  • Operational Excellence: Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with a proactive mindset and the ability to bring structure to complex, fast-moving environments.

  • Communication: Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to act as the connective layer between external partners and internal stakeholders, translating conversations into clear actions.

What you’ll be working on

  • Relationship Management: Managing day-to-day communication with airline partners, handling inbound airline requests (including NDC updates, distribution changes, and operational queries), and ensuring they continue to progress.

  • Reporting & Visibility: Maintaining and building reporting across airline performance metrics, tracking supplier commercial frameworks (including commissions and incentives), and helping the team stay informed.

  • Operational Coordination: Coordinating with internal teams to ensure airline requirements are understood, progressed, and aligned across multiple workstreams.

  • Pipeline Support: Supporting pipeline management by maintaining visibility on prospective airlines and ongoing conversations to keep work moving forward.

  • Process Improvement: Building and improving internal documentation, trackers, and processes across airline partnerships to help the team scale.

A few key pieces of information before applying

  • 📍 Location: We have a hybrid work-from-home policy and require everyone to come to our Shoreditch office on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

  • 📝 Interview Process: Our interview process consists of three stages: a recruiter screen, a hiring manager interview, and a final stage interview.

  • ✔️ Background Checks: If you are successful, all offers will be pending satisfactory background checks (we partner with a third-party provider to do so) and employment references.

Why Join Duffel?

We're a growth-focused team that values open communication, diverse perspectives, and true ownership. We want you to feel empowered in your role, which is why every permanent employee becomes a company shareholder.

🌍 Live Your Best Life

  • Duffel Travel Allowance: We subsidise your wanderlust.

  • Work From Anywhere (60 days): Your office, your rules.

  • Sabbaticals: Long-term loyalty, long-term breaks.

  • Flexible Bank Holidays: Swap holidays to suit your schedule.

🔋 Level Up & Give Back

  • Study Days: Get paid to learn.

  • Volunteering Day: One day a year to save the world.

  • Electric Car & Cycle Schemes: Eco-friendly rides, tax-free prices.

🛡️ The Essentials, Upgraded

  • Family Leave (maternity, paternity and adoption): Big support for life's biggest moments, 26 weeks fully paid.

  • Pensions & Loans: Future-proofing and interest-free commuting.

  • Eye Tests: Keeping your vision (and your style) sharp.

We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe that the key to our success is employing a diverse team, that's why recruitment decisions are only based on your experience and skills. title: Senior People Partner
description: Fonoa is the Tax Operating System for autonomous tax. AI that tracks every rule, acts on every obligation, and proves every decision, built on modular infrastructure. Fonoa's modules cover the full indirect tax lifecycle: tax ID validation, real-time tax determination, e-invoicing, and returns. All on one shared data model and integration, with one audit trail. Each added capability makes the others stronger. Agents monitor obligations, populate returns, catch anomalies and assemble audit packs in seconds. The system does the work. Humans make the calls. That's autonomous tax. Trusted by Canva, Netflix, Spotify, Uber, Zoom and Booking.com . Find out more: www.fonoa.com The role We're looking for a Senior People Partner to sit alongside business leaders at Fonoa and drive high performance across their teams. As Senior People Partner at Fonoa, you'll own the business-facing People relationship for a defined set of leaders and their teams. Real partnership. You'll help managers prevent problems before they escalate, move difficult situations forward when they don't, and build the frameworks that make consistency possible as the company scales. The role spans day-to-day partnering, performance, manager coaching, employee relations, onboarding, career development, culture, and engagement. You'll also provide People coverage for our US employees. The expectation is that you find the 'how' when others default to yes or no. This is a senior IC role on a small, high-calibre People team, reporting to the Chief People Officer. We're looking for commercial credibility, personal gravitas, and the breadth to operate across the full scope of a People function in a fast-scaling business. What you'll do Partner with business leaders. Be the named People partner for a defined set of leaders. First point of contact for people issues, performance conversations, team dynamics, and management challenges. Own the relationship, not just the transaction. Drive performance and accountability. Help managers set clear expectations, have difficult conversations, and act on issues before they become crises. Coach the manager through it. Don't just advise from the side. Own employee relations. Manage ER cases end-to-end across markets, from early intervention through to resolution. Keep things moving, keep things fair, and keep the business out of avoidable risk. Build the people programmes. Design and run the programmes that move the business forward: onboarding, career frameworks, manager training, culture, engagement. Make them real, not decorative. Cover the US & EU. Provide dedicated People partnering for Fonoa's US & EU employees, with working knowledge of US employment law and practices. Shape the function. Help build what the People function looks like as Fonoa scales, and operate as the partner business leaders bring their hardest problems to. What we're looking for Commercial credibility and gravitas. You can hold your own with a CRO, CPO, or founder. You speak the language of the business (performance, output, growth, risk), not the language of HR policy. You've pushed back on a senior leader and can describe specifically what happened. High-growth experience. You've operated in a scaling company where the People function was being built rather than maintained. A 'how, not no' instinct. When the easy answer is yes or no, you look for the third option. You can walk through a specific example where you helped a leader reach a legitimate outcome through a route they hadn't considered. Performance and ER in practice. You've owned performance situations and employee relations cases end-to-end, not just advised on them. You can describe how you support the manager, keep momentum, and bring cases to resolution across multiple jurisdictions. Programme design from scratch. You've built at least one people programme from a blank page, not inherited and maintained one. You can describe the problem, the design, the buy-in, and what changed. Breadth across the People function. Meaningful work across at least two of: performance frameworks, career development, L&D, onboarding, or culture programmes. Range, not depth in one specialism. Strong context-switching. You can manage active situations across multiple teams without dropping things, with a clear method for triaging what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait. Working knowledge of US and UK/EU employment. Enough to be the first point of contact for employees and managers across markets without escalating every question to legal. Fonoa is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Fonoa's modules cover the full indirect tax lifecycle: tax ID validation, real-time tax determination, e-invoicing, and returns. All on one shared data model and integration, with one audit trail. Each added capability makes the others stronger.

Agents monitor obligations, populate returns, catch anomalies and assemble audit packs in seconds. The system does the work. Humans make the calls. That's autonomous tax.

Trusted by Canva, Netflix, Spotify, Uber, Zoom and Booking.com.

Find out more: www.fonoa.com

The role

As Tax Engine Strategic Lead at Fonoa, you'll own the product strategy and technical direction of the Tax Engine. You'll translate deep, hands-on experience across multiple tax engines and tax-product organisations into a clear point of view on what Fonoa's Tax Engine should become, where it should compete, and how content and AI scale together.

The role spans product vision, content strategy, competitive judgement, and tax credibility for the build. You'll operate through the Tax Engine PM and the engineering team, not through customer projects, and not by managing a team of implementers.

This is a Director-equivalent IC role, strategic and deeply hands-on, reporting to the Chief Tax Officer. We're looking for cross-engine pattern recognition, calm under pressure, and the seniority to operate as the PM's tax-domain equal.

What you'll do

  • Own the Tax Engine product vision. Execute the point of view on what Tax Engine 2.0 looks like: how it differentiates in a mature competitive market, how it leverages Fonoa's AI positioning, and what the 18-month build sequence should be. Own the narrative the PM and engineering team build against.

  • Drive content strategy and velocity. Define how tax content (rates, rules, jurisdictions, scenarios) is sourced, validated, structured, and scaled.

  • Partner with the PM as a tax-domain equal. Own the tax half of every prioritisation, design, and trade-off conversation. The PM doesn't translate tax into product. You already speak both.

  • Hold the tax bar for the product. Act as the senior tax authority for Tax Engine inside Fonoa. Sign off on design decisions, content from external partners, and edge cases engineering or PM can't resolve alone. Bring a sharp, competitive view to product reviews, not just when asked.

  • Direct the central tax research and content development function into Tax Engine. Define what support Tax Engine requires from this team (projects, content reviews, scenario testing) and ensure that work consistently meets the quality bar required by the product.

About you

  • Multi-product, multi-vendor tax engine experience (non-negotiable). You've worked on or with more than one tax engine in the indirect tax space. Pattern recognition across products is what makes this profile rare. Single-vendor backgrounds, however senior, don't meet the bar.

  • 10+ years in indirect tax or tax technology. Enough seniority to have seen multiple product cycles, multiple market shifts, and multiple failure modes. This is a judgement seat, not a skills one.

  • Product-leaning, hands-on at seniority. The strongest backgrounds combine vendor product teams, top-tier indirect tax technology consulting, or in-house at a global digital platform that built or heavily customised its own tax engine. You can still go deep on a specific design decision or edge case. Pure managerial profiles who've stopped touching the work won't pass the panel.

  • A real view on AI in content. You can articulate where AI adds genuine leverage in content generation, validation, and maintenance, and where deterministic infrastructure must still own the answer. Not buzzword-level.

  • Product judgement under constraint. Given a Tax Engine 2.0 prompt, you can structure a response: what to build first, what to deliberately not build, and why. You reason from customer and competitive position, not from tax theory.

  • PM partnership and calm under pressure. You operate as a tax-domain equal to the PM, not as an oracle or a gatekeeper. Grounded and clear-headed when everyone around you is sprinting.

As part of the recruitment process at Fonoa, we process your personal data in accordance with our Privacy Notice for Job Applicants. This notice explains how and why your data is collected and used, and how you can contact us if you have any concerns.

Agents monitor obligations, populate returns, catch anomalies and assemble audit packs in seconds. The system does the work. Humans make the calls. That’s autonomous tax.

We operate across 120+ countries, with clients going live in weeks, if not days.
Trusted by Canva, Netflix, Spotify, Uber, Zoom and Booking.com.

Find out more: www.fonoa.com

The Role
We're looking for a Revenue AI & Automation Architect to design and scale the systems that power Fonoa's go-to-market organisation.

This role combines GTM systems, automation, data architecture, and AI implementation. You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations to improve how information moves through the business and automate work that teams currently do manually.

You'll own the architecture, integrations, workflows, and AI tooling that support our commercial teams. The goal is simple: build systems that scale, improve decision-making, and reduce operational complexity.
This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys solving business problems through technology and wants to play a key role in how Fonoa grows.

What You'll Do

AI & Automation

  • Build AI-powered workflows that automate account research, lead qualification, forecasting support, customer health analysis, and renewal preparation

  • Connect AI models and automation tools to live business systems and operational data

  • Identify repetitive processes that can be automated and implement solutions that deliver measurable productivity gains

  • Evaluate emerging AI technologies and determine where they can create practical business value

GTM Systems & Architecture

  • Design and maintain the systems architecture that supports our commercial organisation

  • Build scalable workflows that separate data, business logic, and user experience

  • Reduce tooling complexity, integration debt, and manual operational work

  • Establish standards for system reliability, monitoring, and maintainability


Data & Integrations

  • Own the design of the revenue data model across accounts, contacts, opportunities, customer lifecycle events, and revenue data

  • Manage integrations between Salesforce, marketing platforms, data warehouses, enrichment providers, and AI tooling

  • Ensure data quality, governance, and operational visibility across the GTM stack

  • Create trusted data foundations that support reporting, automation, and decision-making


Business Partnership

  • Translate commercial strategy into scalable systems and workflows

  • Partner with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partnerships, Finance, and Product

  • Influence the tools we buy, the systems we build, and how automation becomes part of day-to-day execution

  • Act as a technical partner to business stakeholders, balancing short-term needs with long-term scalability


What We're Looking For

Required

  • 5+ years in GTM Engineering, Revenue Operations, Revenue Systems, Business Systems, or a similar technical role

  • Strong Salesforce experience, with expertise extending beyond administration

  • Experience designing and managing complex business system integrations

  • Experience deploying AI-powered workflows, automations, agents, or model-driven applications into production environments

  • Strong data modelling and systems design skills

  • Ability to move comfortably between strategic planning and hands-on implementation


Strong Signals

  • Experience building with LLMs, AI APIs, or modern automation platforms

  • Experience with tools such as n8n, Clay, Make, Zapier, Workato, or similar platforms

  • Strong opinions on data governance, automation design, and system architecture

  • Experience scaling systems within a high-growth B2B SaaS company

  • Experience working across multiple GTM functions rather than supporting a single team


What This Role Is Not

  • A Salesforce Administrator role with a different title

  • A reporting and dashboard-focused operations role

  • A project management position coordinating technical work

  • An AI experimentation role without implementation ownership

  • A prompt engineering role disconnected from operational outcomes


Why Join Fonoa?
We're building a modern, AI-enabled operating system for tax. Internally, we're applying the same principles: modularity, automation, observability, and intelligence.


This is an opportunity to design the systems, automations, and AI workflows that support Fonoa's growth. You'll have significant influence over our commercial technology stack and the freedom to implement solutions that create measurable business impact.


If you're excited about combining systems thinking, automation, data, and AI to solve real operational problems, we'd love to hear from you.
